case_name: Muralidhar Ghadei vs Smt. Sumitra Ghadei And Anr.
facts_of_case: Petitioner married respondent in 1964, but they separated. Petitioner later married again. Respondent claimed maintenance from petitioner due to his second marriage.

legal_principles.principle: A wife is entitled to be maintained with dignity of a wife and as Justice Fazl Ali said, the salutory provisions of the Code are not merely meant to provide a wife with food, clothing and lodging as if she is only a chattel.
legal_principles.held: The immortal bird of India. Kalidass brought out through the lips of king Aja in Raghubansam the concept of a wife as 'GRUHINI SACHIBA SAKHl MITTHAH, PRIYA SHISYA......', i.e. that the wife is a partner to the husband and is his advisor, his friend and his dearest disciple

legal_principles.principle: The right of the wife to refuse to live with the husband in case of his second marriage is not confined to the offer of the husband to maintain her only after an order Under Section 125(1), Cr PC has been passed.
legal_principles.held: Indeed there is no reason as to why a distinction should be maintained between a wife who desires to file a petition to claim maintenance on the ground of the husband's second marriage and the wife whose husband has contracted a second marriage after an order of maintenance has been passed and makes an offer to maintain the wife but she refuses to live with him in view of a second marriage.

outcome.final_order: Maintenance of Rs. 300/- per month to the opposite party No. 1 and Rs. 200/- per month to the opp party No. 2, the daughter through her, was granted.
